rationale: The resolver half of bugs_open/334, and the last live conflict class blocking RFC_029 step 5. complete_work_item declares commit_sha Optional (load_work_item_actions.go:56) and writes it into the work item's result (line 937), but NO live step config wired it - so it arrived via findFieldRecursive, the whole-tree search. Inside build-dispatch-loop's multi-iteration loop the tree accumulates one handler result per iteration, each with a different sha, so every completion is a genuine conflict decided by sort order. THIS IS NOT MERELY 'RIGHT BY LUCK', which is what this lane believed a day ago: item cc1db035 (a tool-generator add_tool) carries a result.commit_sha although tool-generator CANNOT produce one - 8 orchestrations all-time, ZERO carrying commit_sha anywhere - because its parent loop's iteration 0 was a section-editor item and the search reached into handler_result_0 and glued ITERATION 0's COMMIT ONTO ITERATION 1's UNRELATED ITEM. So the flip ends a cross-item misattribution class, not just a wrong choice. WHY `?` AND NOT `!` OR A PLAIN WIRE, measured on live traffic 2026-08-21: of 31 recent bdl runs carrying a handler_result, 29 have the key at handler_result.response.commit_sha and 2 do not - a page-build-handler early exit whose response holds only site_record, and a page-rerender whose deploy_result produced no commit. Both are legitimate absences. STRICT would turn them into hard extraction failures, which is not hypothetical: migration 496 wired a different field strictly this morning and every plain add_tool died at save_tool while its work item read complete (hotfixed by 532, to `?`). A PLAIN wire resolves when the path exists and FALLS BACK TO THE SEARCH when it does not, i.e. it guesses on exactly the runs that matter. `?` is the only spelling meaning 'the handler's own reply, or nothing'. ABSENCE IS SAFE, read at the consumer: complete_work_item writes the field only when non-empty (`if sha := inputs.Get("commit_sha"); sha != ""`), so absent means the key is simply not written - no empty string persisted - and `result!` already maps the whole handler_result into result, which still contains the sha at its own path, so the top-level copy is a convenience duplicate. THE GUARD IS THE POINT OF THE FILE. The precise regression this could cause is a handler that DOES commit but does not expose it at response.commit_sha silently ceasing to record result.commit_sha. Nine handlers were standardised for this by the bugs_open/306 lane (519-536). A hand-typed list of those nine would be a snapshot of one census - the defect migration 516 had to be rebuilt to remove - so this file DERIVES the ready-set at apply time: a handler must expose commit_sha if its OWN orchestrations can produce one AND it appears as a live handler_agent. 'Can produce' is a property of the HANDLER; 'an item recorded one' is a property of the RESOLVER BEING REMOVED and counts the contamination above as a requirement - that distinction cost this lane a false positive (tool-generator) earlier the same day. ON ITS FIRST DRY RUN THE GUARD REFUSED, naming content-feed-orchestrator: 17/17 of its own orchestrations carry a commit, it has its own commit_news and commit_rss git_commit steps, it is a live handler_agent, and its complete step is still output_fields. BOTH prior censuses missed it - the structural one and the demand one - and the guard did not. Reported to the standardisation lane; this migration stays UNAPPLIED until it passes. Stated in the file: expect tool-generator to show NO commit_sha after this applies, because it never had one of its own, so nobody reads that drop as a regression.

plan.summary: Declare commit_sha on build-dispatch-loop's mark_complete with the `?` marker so the loop stops resolving it by whole-tree search, gated by a guard that derives the required handler set at apply time and refuses while any commit-producing live handler is unconverted.

edits.rationale: Adds `"commit_sha?": "handler_result.response.commit_sha"` to the nested mark_complete step, located by RECURSIVE DISCOVERY (it lives at workflow.steps.process_item.config.sub_workflow.steps.mark_complete, invisible to a top-level jsonb_each census - 516's lesson). Guards: refuses while any commit-producing live handler is unconverted, naming it; refuses if ZERO agents expose commit_sha (the standardisation is absent and the wire would name a path nothing produces); refuses on an existing commit_sha/commit_sha!/commit_sha? key rather than fighting another author's choice. VERIFY is a DO block asserting the wire and the snapshot row.

Dry run 2026-08-21: REFUSED on content-feed-orchestrator, which is the guard working.

Its header states what rolling back RESTORES - bugs_open/334 including the cross-item misattribution - so the decision is informed rather than reflexive. Same recursive discovery as the apply, so it cannot miss a wire written at a path a typed list did not anticipate.

Live step config read by recursive walk 2026-08-21: build-dispatch-loop's only complete_work_item step is at workflow.steps.process_item.config.sub_workflow.steps.mark_complete with config {result!, error_step, work_item_id!} - no commit_sha wire of any spelling.

Live traffic 2026-08-21: 29 of 31 recent bdl runs carry handler_result.response.commit_sha (real shas, multiple handlers incl. page-rerender, css-patch-agent, image-build-handler); the 2 without are a page-build-handler early exit (response holds only site_record) and a page-rerender whose deploy_result produced no commit.

All nine standardised handlers expose commit_sha via result_mapping from their own internal paths (asset-deployer deploy_result.response.data.commit_sha, page-build-handler deploy_result.response.commit_sha, section-editor git_result.response.data.commit_sha, etc.) - read from live definitions, which is why one wire path serves all of them.

Guard dry run 2026-08-21 against live data: REFUSED naming content-feed-orchestrator (17/17 own orchestrations carry a commit; commit_news and commit_rss git_commit steps; live handler_agent; complete step still output_fields).
plan.risks: The wire is UNAPPLIED and will stay so until the guard passes - content-feed-orchestrator needs the same result_mapping conversion the other nine had, which is the standardisation lane's half and has been reported to them. Honest read on that gap: its single dispatched item records no sha today, so wiring now would take nothing from it; the guard is deliberately conservative and refuses on 'can commit' rather than 'is currently recording', because the second is a property of the mechanism being removed. The guard's producer probe is a coarse text match over the handler's own collected_data, so a tree that merely RECEIVED a sha could over-include a handler - the failure direction is deliberate (over-inclusion blocks the apply loudly; under-inclusion drops a field silently), and tool-generator is correctly excluded because the probe is scoped to owner_agent_type. After apply, expect tool-generator's commit_sha to stop appearing, which is the fix rather than a regression, and verification needs fresh multi-iteration loop demand plus an instrument-alive control from a class this migration does not silence.
